characters.name: Nemo
characters.arc: Protagonist — wants to sink the slaving fleet regardless of cost —  — Active Arc: In Chapter 10, Nemo refuses medical aid to Broussard during the storm to maintain operational security, choosing the mission over the man.
characters.voice: speaks in commands and silence, treats men as instruments,

characters.name: Anselm Broussard
characters.arc: Accomplice — wants to die with purpose

characters.name: Ayaanle Ibrahim
characters.arc: Accomplice — wants justice for her family —  — Active Arc: In Chapter 7, Ayaanle charts the route through the Somali reefs despite Nemo’s order to hold position, trusting her memory of the currents over his memory of the battle.
characters.voice: precise, navigational, reads currents like text,

characters.name: Lord Percival Thorne
characters.arc: Antagonist — wants to preserve the concession

settings.name: The Aletheia
settings.description: A claustrophobic, copper-smelling iron lung buried in the silt, illuminated only by the bioluminescent pulse of the thermal vents; it smells of ozone and old blood.

settings.name: Stone Town, Zanzibar
settings.description: A city of carved doors and salt rot, where the heat presses against the skin like a hand and the air tastes of clove and decay.

settings.name: Pemba Channel
settings.description: Open water marked by the white foam of coral heads, where the current pulls with the certainty of fate.

settings.name: Gulf of Oman
settings.description: A violent crucible of monsoon winds and black water, where the horizon disappears and only the compass remains.

plot_points.description: Nemo surfaces off Zanzibar, recruiting Broussard from the hotel floor using the promise of a clean death.
Ayaanle joins the crew, revealing she knows the slavers’ route before Nemo asks.
The first strike on the dhow near Pemba succeeds, but Nemo finds children among the cargo, fracturing his moral certainty.
The British Consul demands Broussard’s head; Broussard realizes he is expendable.
The engagement in the Gulf of Oman destroys the fleet but traps the Aletheia; Nemo chooses fire over capture.
Ayaanle escapes with the ledger; Nemo remains in the deep, his fortune transferred to her.

voice: Third-person limited, alternating between Nemo, Broussard, and Ayaanle; past tense; prose that favors the weight of water over the lightness of air, echoing Melville’s moral gravity and Conrad’s psychological depth.
